topic: Natural Language Processing in Electronic Health Records in Relation to Healthcare Decision-making: A Systematic Review
topic_definition: Stage 2 canonical eligibility, source-faithful to the original paper's screening criteria. Eligible studies are peer-reviewed journal articles or full conference papers using ML- or DL-based models or frameworks designed solely for EHR analysis, focused on analyzing or identifying clinical narratives through ML or DL methods.
summary: Stage 2 canonical criteria restated from criteria_mds/2306.12834.md; publication-time filtering is handled by cutoff_jsons/2306.12834.json.

summary_topics.description: Natural Language Processing in Electronic Health Records in Relation to Healthcare Decision-making: A Systematic Review

required.criterion: Paper is a peer-reviewed journal article or a full conference paper, not an abstract-only publication.
Paper uses an ML- or DL-based model or framework designed solely for analyzing EHRs.
Paper focuses on analyzing or identifying clinical narratives through ML or DL methods.

Paper describes at least one covered topic type in the context of EHR or medical text: ML/DL-based free-text classification, word embeddings, automatic clinical-narrative summarization, healthcare dialogue systems, medical concept embedding, delirium risk identification, ICD-9 multilabel classification, clinical entity recognition, or ML/DL architectures for EHRs.

exclusion_criteria.criterion: Preprints, preliminary works, and works without peer review are excluded.
Full-text articles failing the source review's quality examination are excluded; the source criteria do not define a concrete quality rubric, so no additional rubric is invented here.
